newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's foreign minister mulls resignation.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's foreign minister mulls resignation.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Friday Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler was considering resigning over opposition charges that he was ineffectual.
"The minister yesterday confirmed to me that he was seriously considering it and we agreed that we would talk about it next week," Drnovsek told a news conference.
"It is very hard for him to bear incorrect attacks," Drnovsek added, saying he did not favour a Thaler resignation.
The Foreign Ministry had no comment on the minister's future, saying no news on the matter could be expected before Tuesday, when Thaler is due back from holiday.

Drnovsek's comment came only three days after Slovenia's main opposition party, the Social Democrats, had called for a parliamentary debate on the government's effectiveness. Such a debate, which could lead to a no-confidence vote, is expected to take place in September.

The party said one of the reasons for calling the debate was the foreign minister's ineffectual performance. It claimed that he was partly responsible for the fact that Slovenia had had to change its constitution to enable foreigners to buy land before it could become an associate member of the European Union.

Thaler had already threatened to resign once this month if parliament failed to amend the constitution and ratify the EU association agreement by July 15. The parliament later did both in time for Thaler's deadline.
Thaler, 35, a member of Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats, has held the post since late February, when the new government took office following the November general elections.

He held the same position for over a year in the previous government but was ousted in May 1996 by a no-confidence vote in parliament, accused of failing to carry out effective negotiations on Slovenia's associate membership of the EU.
